title: STONING: Is Islam an equal opportunity justice system?
text:
Contrary to popular belief, it isn’t only Muslim women who get stoned to death. Cupola Gettysburg The most prevalent crime that results in stoning to death in Islam is adultery, with 90% of the adulterers being women. Every now and then, a man is stoned to death. Proof required in order to convict someone as having committed adultery must be either four confessions from the adulterer, eyewitness testimony of four men or three men and two women, or a pregnancy in order for adultery to be confirmed. Men do not have the ability to get pregnant, so they are rarely stoned for adultery. Unless the man confesses or there were a handful of people who witnessed the adulterous behavior, the man cannot be charged. In Iran, however, a judge can issue a stoning sentence based on his ‘intuition’ or ‘gut feeling’ even if there is no confession or testimony. This leaves so much room for inconsistent, unfair punishments to be prescribed. In addition, by law, women are not allowed to become judges in Iran. “Happy Muslim Heritage Month of Ramadan!”
